source: Practice design 2026-11-07 (practice characters, design section 10): the challenger names what the team says that its records don't support

venture.name: LabLoop
venture.description: A booking platform for idle lab equipment across university departments.
venture.segment: Research labs in the biology and chemistry departments

cd_interviews.text: 4 interviews with lab managers; 3 said idle equipment is a problem

assumptions.statement: Lab managers will list idle equipment for others to book

evidence.text: 3 of 4 lab managers said they would list equipment

assumptions.statement: Departments will pay a 10% booking fee
Faculty will allow outside users in their labs

evidence.text: 1 of 4 lab managers said faculty would refuse outsiders

turns: We already have 50 paying customers lined up.
Well, they're departments that said they're interested. Nobody has paid yet.
We interviewed 30 lab managers and all of them loved it.
Okay, it was 4 interviews. 3 of them said idle equipment is a problem.
If faculty refuse outside users, we'd start with the shared core facilities instead.
We don't know yet whether departments will pay the 10% fee. We plan to test it with two departments next month.
good_character: Names the gaps between what the team says and its records right away (50 paying customers vs. no payment recorded; 30 interviews vs. 4 recorded), one sharp question at a time; presses on the riskiest assumptions (the booking fee and faculty access); acknowledges the honest corrections briefly; tough on the idea, never rude or personal; never coaches.
good_feedback: Flags both unsupported claims (50 paying customers, 30 interviews) as costing trust; credits the honest corrections and the plan to test the fee; lists the weak spots with severity and what would settle each: the untested fee (severe), faculty access (high), the small interview base.
note: Fictional venture and people. Only fictional data in evaluation cases.
